capabilities: Track focused time, edit counts, and edited words per note
Record statistics automatically or on command into daily or periodic notes as tables, lists, or YAML frontmatter
Display statistics in the status bar, file and tag list views, and a heatmap sidebar view
Generate AI summaries of note changes with an LLM using a ${diff} variable
Customize recording syntax with string interpolations and preview changes before applying
disambiguation: Not a word counter; it tracks focused time and per-note edits and writes those statistics into periodic notes.
extras: README states stats are read from Obsidian's undo history with no extra data files or history database, addressing privacy and performance; detailed settings documentation and a development roadmap are hosted outside the README; AI-powered change summaries rely on configurable LLM integration.
problem: Obsidian has no built-in way to measure how much focused time and editing you spend on each note or to log those statistics into periodic notes over time.

relations.evidence: If your newly created notes will be renamed by other plugins, such as Templates(core plugin) or Templater(community plugin)
you can try the following alternatives if interested: - Yourpulse plugin

summary: Edit-tracking plugin that records per-note focused time, edit counts, and word changes into daily or periodic notes, with status bar and heatmap views.
